title: RPC Invocation engineering rules and evidence boundaries

records.rule: Connect Selector owns route selection and route permissions.
Serialisation Selector owns codec/schema binding, including protobuf.
One protocol-neutral RpcServiceDispatcher owns object/method invocation.
SOAP, JSON-RPC and gRPC retain distinct envelopes and fault/status translations.
Exact allowlisted service+operation maps to registered target/method; no untrusted reflection.
Server callback registration differs from exported client callback address; completion is terminal and single.
No accidental client/bidi support by collecting request messages into an array.
A later stream fault supersedes earlier onNext messages; never claim success from partial delivery.
Authentication/authorization is separate from registry, codec, and HTTP/2 negotiation.
No silent retries/failover for effects or uncertain completion.
Portfolio transfer submitted; receipt not seen at sphere authorship; dev3 gRPC ooRexx callback runtime unqualified.
Published operation -> RPC registered method only; identity authority tied to live HTTPS context and verified per invocation; source adapter v0.1-dev1 is NOT yet runtime/deployment qualified.
